title: Feedback must not look like a button
statement: Make feedback and a guide's speech look unlike controls, keeping button styles for what acts when pressed, since learners may try to tap anything drawn like a button.
example: One lesson used four button styles with no rule tying them to meaning.
detail: A supplied UI review of a Grade 3 lesson found the guide's speech bubble drawn as a green outlined rounded rectangle, the same look as the lesson's pill buttons, and four button styles in one lesson with no rule connecting them to meaning (`grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/gold-standard/aladdin-p1-ui-review.reference.md`, lines 28 and 33). The project kept the avatar and readable text but drew replies with a thin verdict rule, square corners and a transparent ground, keeping the action pill for deliberate click controls (`grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/gold-standard/REVIEW-MAPPING.md`, line 18; `grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/gold-standard/STYLE-IMPLEMENTATION-by-residual.md`, line 22).
against: The tap prediction is the review's judgment, not observed with children, and the restyle is a source candidate, "not a deployed or final browser-accepted state" (`grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/gold-standard/STYLE-IMPLEMENTATION-by-residual.md`, line 3); the mapping marks it "Pending visual refinement" (`grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/gold-standard/REVIEW-MAPPING.md`, line 18).

evidence.quote: On `/p3` it is a green outlined rounded rectangle, the same visual language as the "Sound it out" and "The word parts" pills.
A child will try to tap it.
There are four button styles in one lesson and no rule connecting them to meaning.
Reply should retain avatar and readable text with a subtle rule/verdict marker; action pill belongs only to deliberate click controls.
Reply uses a1px bottom verdict rule, square corners, transparent background and500 text.
**E3. Feedback is honest about affordance**: success feedback must never look like another tappable element (doc 1 item 7).
the verdict element has no role=button/cursor-pointer; OWED as a general sweep.
Use borders, spacing and typography to separate feedback and controls.
spoken feedback must not look like another button.
